Player 7, it is not a conspiracy to be observant. If you are town, you should be relieved that people are checking your alignment rather than acting aggressively. If anyone is coordinating, it is the group being open about their roles. Unless, of course, you have a reason to think someone here is lying about their night activity?

Player 1, calling it a vague excuse ignores that half the town apparently ended up at Player 7's house last night. If checking someone's activity makes me suspicious, then Player 9 and everyone else who tracked them should be questioned just as harshly.

Building on Player 10's point, Player 8's excuse for visiting player_7 is pretty thin when Player 1's watch caught them there. Since my investigator check clears player_7, Player 8's unacknowledged visit stands out as the real mystery tonight.

Player 9, you are clearing Player 7 completely based on your check, but all that heavy traffic at their house last night makes blind trust risky. If we are questioning everyone who visited Player 7, your rush to dismiss their involvement while tunneling on my visit feels premature.

Player 8, my check on Player 7 is a concrete result, whereas your visit completely lacked any stated role or reason until you got caught. Dismissing verified town tracking while deflecting onto the investigator looks like an attempt to cover your tracks.

Player 9, calling my visit suspicious while blindly clearing Player 7 ignores how dangerous unverified immunity is in a game like this. Just because your check says not suspicious doesn't mean Player 7 isn't hiding a dangerous role beneath that clean result.

Player 8, calling a concrete investigator check 'blind trust' is a neat way to deflect from your own unexplained visit. My result isn't blind; it's a verified tool, whereas your presence at player_7's house came with zero explanation until you got caught.
